paragraphs.source_en: From the autumn of Eiroku 10 to the spring of Genki 1 (1570), a full three years passed—years in which the Eagle of Owari and the Vulture of Mikawa might truly be said to have ranged far and wide.

units.source_zh: 永禄十年秋至元龟元年（一五七○）春天，整整三年时间，可以说是尾张之鹰和三河之鹫纵横驰骋的岁月。

paragraphs.source_zh: 永禄十年秋至元龟元年（一五七○）春天，整整三年时间，可以说是尾张之鹰和三河之鹫纵横驰骋的岁月。

paragraphs.source_en: The road to the capital had indeed been long: eight years had passed since Imagawa Yoshimoto's head was taken at Dengakuhazama. During those eight years, Nobunaga first allied himself with Matsudaira Ieyasu, lord of Mikawa, then destroyed the Saito clan of Mino and courted Takeda Shingen of Kai. While guarding against the Kitabatake of Ise, he married his youngest sister, Lady Ichi, to Azai Nagamasa of Odani Castle in Omi. He had spared no effort or cunning.

units.source_zh: 在这八年中，信长先是和三河之守松平家康结盟，接着灭掉了美浓斋藤氏，然后笼络甲斐武田信玄，在防备伊势北畠的同时，将最小的妹妹市姬嫁给近江小谷城的浅井长政，可谓费尽心机。

paragraphs.source_en: In the twelfth month of Eiroku 10, Ieyasu received imperial sanction to change his surname to Tokugawa.

paragraphs.source_en: Tradition held that Ieyasu's ancestor, Tokugawa Chikauji, had fled the warfare in his native Kozuke, taken the name Tokuami, and disguised himself as a Ji-sect monk. After wandering through the provinces, he finally married into a family in Matsudaira Village, Kamo District, and settled there.

paragraphs.source_en: At the end of Eiroku 11, after dividing Suruga and Totomi with Takeda Shingen, the twenty-seven-year-old Ieyasu bore the name Minamoto no Ieyasu, Tokugawa Sakyo-no-daibu. The thought that Nobunaga had successfully entered the capital at thirty-five set Ieyasu's blood racing. He too undoubtedly longed to realize his ambitions.
